purpose: Capture-dated facts about the Andalusian Project YouTube channel and the re-uploads that stand in for it. Every row is a Wayback capture that F6 (task 6) already had on disk; no network request was made for this file. Interpretations are held to what a capture can show: a capture records a channel's state, never its operator.

channel.uc_id_status: historical identifier, and a stable one. The videos were removed from the channel around October 2022; the same channel id was re-populated with 84 items by May 2023; those items were gone again by August 2025; and the 2025-08-20 and 2026-08-19 captures plus the controller's 2026-09-27 live check all show the page unavailable with no videos.
channel.do_not_link_reason: two reasons, neither of which requires knowing who controlled the account. (1) The live page is unavailable - the 2026-09-27 live check returned 'This channel is not available.' - and the 2025-08-20 and 2026-08-19 captures show 0 videos, so a link leads a reader nowhere. (2) The 2023 contents are of undetermined authorship, so linking the id would present unverified uploads as his. The id is recorded here as provenance only.
channel.current_state: unavailable (terminal as of the 2026-09-27 live check)

do_not_link.is_his_meaning: unknown - deliberately not asserted in either direction
do_not_link.marker: DO NOT LINK - never link this handle
do_not_link.why_do_not_link: the handle is attached to a channel that shows 0 videos and has reported itself unavailable since the 2025-08-20 capture, and the 84 items visible in the 2023 captures cannot be attributed to Asadullah Ali from the captures alone. The handle is withheld on those two grounds; it is NOT withheld because ownership has been established against him.
do_not_link.provable_timeline: the /channel/UCqYAQa28E9Fbsak6zM4hA3w captures from 2015-06-29 to 2022-03-20 all carry rel=canonical = that same id; the videos were removed around October 2022; the 2023-05-27 /about capture shows the same id re-populated with 84 videos and 15.4K subscribers under the handle @andalusianproject6093; the 2025-08-20 and 2026-08-19 captures show 0 videos; the 2026-09-27 live check reports the channel unavailable.
do_not_link.not_established: who controlled the account in 2023 - Asadullah Ali himself, or a third party with access to it. The captures cannot settle this, so no claim is made either way.

account_control.statement: YouTube does not transfer a channel (UC) id between accounts, so whatever was uploaded to UCqYAQa28E9Fbsak6zM4hA3w in 2023 was uploaded through the same account that held the channel before October 2022.
account_control.what_the_2023_items_are_consistent_with: a re-upload or a return of material to the existing account. The 84 videos in the 2023-05-27 /about capture are consistent with that; the captures are also consistent with material he had not previously published, so consistency is not confirmation.
account_control.what_cannot_be_determined_from_captures: who operated that account in 2023. A capture shows the account's state, not its operator. This file therefore makes no claim about who held the account in 2023, in either direction.

preservation.note: the channel page is gone or unavailable; the archive is the preservation. Mirror URLs are attached to the entry they duplicate (constraint 5) and are never counted as separate works. Counts here are read from _data/videos.json at the time this file was written (56 archive.org entries, 36 attached mirror URLs, 12 catalogue-only live entries). The do-not-link rule above is link hygiene, not a claim about ownership: the archive stands on those files, not on who controlled the account in 2023.
preservation.see_also: preservation_record (the page-facing statement of the same counts, read 2026-09-27) and standing_reuploads

identity_continuity.statement: The channel id UCqYAQa28E9Fbsak6zM4hA3w is the same id in every capture on disk, from 2015-06-29 to 2026-08-19. Nothing in the captures shows it being replaced, and YouTube does not transfer a channel (UC) id between accounts, so no account swap can hide behind it.
how_the_continuity_is_evidenced: captures 2015-06-29, 2018-05-24, 2019-10-30, 2020-10-07 (x4), 2020-11-11, 2021-07-14, 2021-09-04 and 2022-03-20 carry a rel=canonical link whose href is the channel's own /channel/UCqYAQa28E9Fbsak6zM4hA3w path - 11 of the 14 non-empty page captures (the archived path is recorded as text so no live channel URL is emitted)
the 2023 captures carry the same rel=canonical while the channel header's canonicalBaseUrl is the handle /@andalusianproject6093 - the handle changed, the id did not
the 2025-08-20 and 2026-08-19 captures are served under the same id and the same handle, and both return 'This channel is not available.'

in the four head-only captures (20180822164640, 20180822164710, 20190321101143, 20201011145042) the archived head is truncated before the canonical tag, but each capture record's url field and the subscription button's data-channel-external-id both carry the same id

canonical_link.why_absent: those four are head-only captures: the Wayback record stored the document head and no body, and the head as archived stops before the canonical link. This is a property of the capture, not evidence of a different channel - the same captures name the same id in their url field and on the subscription button.
canonical_link.why_not_retrievable: Wayback returned 0 bytes, 0 bytes and 21 bytes respectively. They are listed so the gaps are not mistaken for losses of evidence.

subscriber_series_note: One row per capture that carries the channel's OWN subscriber count - never another channel's. The pre-2023 counts are read from the branded subscription button (the one whose data-channel-external-id is UCqYAQa28E9Fbsak6zM4hA3w); the 2019-10-30 and later counts are read from the channel's own c4TabbedHeaderRenderer. Several of these captures also print other channels' counts in the same page (up to 1.01 million on the 2023-03-15 capture); none of them are this channel's. Numbers are transcribed exactly as YouTube rounded them, so 11.2K means 11,200 +/- 50, not an exact count. Captures with no readable count (2021-07-14 /community) are absent from this series and are recorded in the timeline instead.

preservation_record.headline: The archive is the durable copy, not YouTube.
preservation_record.how_split: 56 entries carry an archive.org file (archive_org_id + filename + size_bytes) in the andalusian-project collection; the other 12 survive only as live re-uploads elsewhere and are marked with kind (appearance 8, clip 4) and a named source. All 68 entries are counted exactly once.
preservation_record.transcripts: 56 baseline transcripts - one per archive.org entry, all 56 covered by _data/transcript_coverage.json - produced from 38 whisper-base-local passes, 1 whisper-tiny re-mux and 18 YouTube auto-caption files (one French, the rest English). The 12 catalogue-only entries carry transcripts: 0, which means 'no transcript attached', not 'no transcript exists': G47Stp3pLss's caption capture is preserved in transcript_coverage.json and deliberately not attached, because the entry is catalogue-only by design.
preservation_record.transcripts_reparented: 10 caption files from duplicate re-uploads were re-parented onto the archive.org entry they duplicate (alternates in transcript_coverage.json, reparented_at 2026-09-27) and are flagged superseded. No transcript text was deleted: the capture files are retained and the text sits in the alternate rows.
preservation_record.mirror_urls: 36 live re-upload URLs are attached to the 30 archive.org entries they duplicate, and are never counted as separate videos (counting-constraint 5). All 68 entries carry the mirror_urls key, empty where a video has no known re-upload.
preservation_record.superseded_duplicates: _data/superseded_videos.json preserves 12 removed duplicate rows in full: title, live uploader, HTTP status, the baseline entry each duplicates, the match basis, duration evidence where it exists (3 of 12), and the verbatim superseded_record. 11 of the 12 are now carried as mirror_urls on the twin they duplicate; the twelfth, G47Stp3pLss, was restored as a distinct counted entry by user decision on 2026-09-27. This file is an audit trail, not a deletion.
preservation_record.caveat: these counts are the state of the data files on 2026-09-27. The final recount is a separate approval gate (Task 9); if it changes a number, this record changes with it.

standing_reuploads.what_this_is: Third-party YouTube channels that currently host re-uploads of recordings this archive catalogued. Every entry below was checked live by F6 on 2026-09-27 and returned HTTP 200. They are re-uploads of the archived recordings - none of them is the original channel, and none of them is operated by this archive.
standing_reuploads.counting_rule: a re-upload is never counted as a separate video. Where it duplicates a catalogued recording, its URL is attached to that entry as a mirror_url; where it is the only surviving copy of a recording, the video is catalogued once in its own right.

totals.breakdown: 36 attached as mirror_urls + 12 superseded-row audit entries + 12 catalogue-only entries (G47Stp3pLss appears in both the superseded audit trail and the catalogue, so the distinct count is 47)

do_not_link_rule.statement: Three things are never linked from this archive, and the reasons are operational, not rhetorical.

rules.why: it is unavailable. The 2026-09-27 live check returned 'This channel is not available.', and the 2025-08-20 and 2026-08-19 captures show 0 videos, so a link leads a reader nowhere.

rules.rule: recorded as text only, never as a link
rules.why: the id is a historical identifier and nothing more. Every Wayback URL for the pre-2023 captures embeds that dead channel path, so those captures are cited here by their capture timestamp and archived path instead, and the id is printed as plain text.

the 84-85 items in the 2023 captures are of undetermined authorship, so linking it would present unverified uploads as his. It is also attached to a channel that shows 0 videos and has reported itself unavailable since 2025-08-20. It is NOT withheld because ownership has been established against him - it is withheld because it cannot be established for him either.

do_not_link_rule.what_is_not_being_claimed: The do-not-link rule is link hygiene. It is not a finding about who controlled the account in 2023, and the archive's standing does not depend on it: the archive stands on its own files, not on the channel.

evidence_files.staging_is_temporary: Every capture behind this file was read from a local staging area that is gitignored and deleted after the final phase. Nothing on the public page depends on those files existing: each claim carries its capture timestamp and, where the archived URL is not a dead channel path, a Wayback link. The local payload filename and the archived path stay recorded per row in this data file and are never printed on the page, so any claim can still be re-checked against the Wayback Machine by timestamp.
evidence_files.how_to_recheck_a_row: take the capture timestamp (e.g. 20220320030541), open the Wayback Machine for that timestamp, and read the channel's own header. Sub-page paths and query strings varied between captures (?app=desktop, ?disable_polymer=1, /videos, /about, /community, /featured) - that variation is YouTube's, not the archive's, and the canonical id is the same in every one of them.
staging_paths_cited: _staging/videos/discovery/mirror_pages/*.raw (the 2022-2026 captures, own_root / own_about / own_channels / ap6093_* / own_featured / own_videos2025)
_staging/videos/manifest.json (the exact archived URL behind every capture above)
_staging/videos/discovery/oembed_results.json (F6's 239-id oEmbed sweep: uploader and channel handle behind every live re-upload)
